issues.title: ARCH-01 — Mobile-First Product Architecture & Surface Boundaries
issues.body:
**Priority:** P0 — Product Architecture Decision

## Decision
CITYWALK is now a **mobile-first traveler product**.

The primary traveler experience is delivered through:
- **iOS**
- **Android**

The Web application remains important, but it is no longer required to mirror every traveler-facing mobile feature.

## Product surface model

### 1. iOS + Android — Primary traveler product
Core traveler capabilities belong here by default:
- multi-city discovery
- Build My Walk
- return-by planning
- interests and walking preference
- current/manual start and destination
- route preview
- active trip/navigation
- GPS/location permissions
- maps
- audio
- verified CITYWALK AI Guide
- Skip / Shorten / Add stop / Take me back
- adaptive route behavior
- saved trips
- trip completion
- account/profile
- native review prompts
- mobile payments where enabled
- future offline/native capabilities

New core traveler features should be designed **mobile-first** and implemented for both iOS and Android unless a platform exception is explicitly documented.

### 2. Public Web — Acquisition, SEO, sharing and preview
The public Web surface exists primarily for:
- CITYWALK marketing landing page
- SEO city pages
- searchable trip/itinerary content
- city discovery pages
- shareable place/walk links
- lightweight product previews/demos where useful
- App Store / Google Play conversion
- partner/hotel/creator landing pages
- legal pages
- contact/support
- optional account/purchase management where useful

Web does **not** need full parity with the native active-trip experience.

Examples of traveler features that are mobile-first and may be omitted from Web:
- rich active walking controls
- native navigation lifecycle
- background trip experience
- native permission UX
- store review prompts
- native purchase flows
- device-specific offline behavior

### 3. Admin Web — Operations platform
The secure Admin Web remains a first-class product surface for CITYWALK operations:
- cities
- places
- tours
- media
- translations
- audio
- verified sources
- publishing workflow
- users
- analytics/product health
- commerce/entitlements
- feedback/bugs
- operational tools

Content/operations features are Web Admin by default and do not require iOS/Android equivalents.

## Shared architecture
Even though surfaces differ, CITYWALK keeps one shared backend/domain architecture.

Prefer sharing:
- city/place/tour domain models
- planner logic
- route eligibility/ranking
- return-by calculations
- trip adaptation rules
- verified AI context and eligibility
- auth/account rules
- entitlements
- analytics event taxonomy
- localization/content contracts
- public APIs

Do not create separate business-rule implementations for iOS and Android without a technical reason.

## Platform requirement rule
Every ticket should explicitly classify its surfaces:

- **Mobile Core:** iOS + Android required
- **Public Web:** required / optional / not applicable
- **Admin Web:** required / not applicable

A feature is not required on every surface merely for parity.

## Examples

| Capability | iOS | Android | Public Web | Admin Web |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Build My Walk | Required | Required | Optional preview | No |
| Active Trip | Required | Required | Not required | No |
| GPS/navigation | Required | Required | Optional/light | No |
| City SEO page | No | No | Required | No |
| Landing page | No | No | Required | No |
| Content editing | No | No | No | Required |
| User analytics dashboard | No | No | No | Required |
| Legal/privacy pages | Linked | Linked | Required canonical URLs | No |

## Launch strategy
1. Complete native CITYWALK V2 parity on iOS + Android.
2. Ship TestFlight + Google Play closed/internal beta.
3. Complete analytics across mobile and Web acquisition surfaces.
4. Complete Admin users/product dashboard.
5. Finish Lübeck content quality and one second-city proof.
6. Publish marketing/SEO Web layer.
7. Complete legal/observability/store metadata.
8. Public iOS + Android release.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Product docs/tickets no longer require full traveler Web parity.
- [ ] Core traveler features are iOS + Android first.
- [ ] Public Web scope is acquisition/SEO/share/legal/preview.
- [ ] Admin Web remains the content/operations surface.
- [ ] Shared business/domain logic remains reusable.
- [ ] New tickets classify required surfaces explicitly.
- [ ] Mobile analytics use the same event taxonomy as Web acquisition analytics where applicable.
- [ ] Localization strategy remains shared even when UI implementations differ.

## Definition of Done
This ticket becomes the canonical architecture decision referenced by PM, launch, QA, mobile, landing, analytics and content tickets.
